A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Atom Theory research, with matching authors, methods and overlapping experiments. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and figures, tables and equations can be matched despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original representation-shift measurements, SAE reconstruction and stability results, scaling experiments and entity case studies in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds training-source and activation-function comparisons, sample-size sensitivity experiments and quantitative monosemanticity evaluation.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains a single-layer SAE with coordinate-wise JumpReLU thresholds and a reconstruction-plus-L1 objective. The AIP framework and encoder/decoder parameterization are retained. Renaming these models TSAEs and moving their training equations to Appendix C.3 do not change the method.

E1.justification: v2 extends TSAE training beyond entity-knowledge activations to natural-text Wikipedia activations and MATH500 mathematical-reasoning activations (Appendix C.1, Table 2). These add distinct input domains to the reconstruction experiments. The main CounterFact/WikiData studies and language-model families are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated ReLU SAE comparator against JumpReLU TSAEs on Gemma2-2B layers 5–13 (Table 3); v1 discussed ReLU theoretically without reporting this comparison. Neurons also appear explicitly in the faithfulness comparison. The GemmaScope and LlamaScope configurations are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include GPT-5.2 semantic-category scoring of ten sampled units per selected layer, training-source comparisons matched in model/data scale, and sample-size sensitivity checks from 128 to 4,096 entities. The scaling-data description changes from up to 73,728 collected activations to a 1.9B-sample pool, although the heatmap is unchanged; this does not establish that the retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of threshold activation necessity, training-source dependence and representation-shift sensitivity to sample size, plus quantitative monosemanticity analysis and a Hawaii–Honolulu case. Existing hyperparameter, encoder–decoder alignment and approximate-orthogonality analyses are retained. The six Mac OS case tables are removed, while the Beijing cases remain.

E5.justification: v2 introduces means and standard errors over sampled representational units for monosemanticity scores (Appendix C.7; Figures 6 and 43). v1 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. Neither version reports repeated-training seed counts; the new error bars describe variation across sampled units.

E6.justification: New results include training-source reconstruction scores of 99.84%, 99.86% and 99.89% (Table 2), ReLU comparisons and monosemanticity rankings. The main atom reconstruction means remain 99.92%, 99.93% and 99.85%; the reported Gemma2-9B stability summary changes from 99.88% to 99.87%. v1's detailed coherence/sparsity columns, average-L0 plots, Mac OS cases and some model-layer angle plots are removed.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the restrictive sparsity assumption with a sparsity-level definition that stipulates no particular regime, and removes v1's kernel/Hilbert-space derivation from Appendix C.6. More consequentially, Theorem 3.11 replaces Theorem 10's recovery 'in a probabilistic sense' with unqualified exact recovery, while retaining the probabilistic argument in its proof.

C1.justification: The central Atom Theory, threshold-SAE identifiability and near-perfect reconstruction/stability claims are retained. v2 adds a headline claim that identified atoms exhibit substantially higher monosemanticity. Its emphasis on faithfulness and stability largely reorganizes criteria already evaluated in v1.

C2.justification: Where v1 deliberately avoids subjective semantic interpretation, v2 argues that structural stability is necessary for monosemanticity and interprets judge scores and the Hawaii–Honolulu atom semantically. It also adds cross-source generality claims and critiques conventional SAE capacity selection. The final-layer Llama training-failure limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds hardware and GPU-hour costs, explicit AIP second-moment estimation and non-overlap details, and the semantic judge prompt and sampling instructions. It removes v1's exact CounterFact activation totals and explicit supplementary-reproduction-material statement. The code-access link is retained; the PDFs do not establish a change in actual resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes AIP from Park et al.'s causal inner product and distinguishes its threshold motivation from prior JumpReLU/TopK motivations. It adds citations including Erichson et al., Makhzani and Frey, and Hendrycks et al., while dropping Elhage et al. (2021). The overall neurons-versus-features positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and much of the main narrative are extensively rewritten around defining, evaluating and identifying FRUs. Theory and experiments are reorganized, training equations and analyses move to appendices, and terminology changes to Atom Theory and TSAEs. The ethics/reproducibility and LLM-use sections are replaced or removed.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, adds a framework schematic, recasts reconstruction/stability line plots as radar charts and tables, and adds semantic-score bar charts and ablation displays. Existing alignment and orthogonality figures move to the appendix. Several sparsity plots and case tables are removed, although many retained graphics are identical.

improvement.justification: The new semantic evaluation, targeted ablations and compute disclosures improve empirical support and assessability. However, v2 strengthens the central identifiability theorem to exact recovery without strengthening its probabilistic proof (Appendix A.7), and removes detailed coherence/sparsity results useful for checking stability. These substantive benefits and losses leave the net change in overall quality uncertain.
